html:
Architecture overview

smTO is a model-led agent runtime for durable tool execution and automation. The Controller accepts work and owns its execution history; models propose decisions; registered tools produce observations and effects. A browser displays that state and submits actions. A selected Gateway owns execution on its target computer.

System context and component ownership

flowchart LR U[Browser or API client] -->|Requests and explicit actions| C[Controller] C -->|Status, results and questions| U C -->|Prepared messages and tool schemas| M[Configured model endpoint] M -->|Proposed decisions| C C -->|Scoped target operations| G[Selected Gateway] G -->|Process and provider evidence| C C --> L[Controller-local tool adapters] C --> S[Controller RAM repositories] S --> D[Committed recovery generation] I[Optional inference manager] -.->|Managed endpoint lifecycle| M
Component Owns Does not establish by itself
Browser and API clients User input, selection, drafts and presentation of server state. Accepted task authority or proof that an operation completed.
Controller API and task services Input validation, accepted configuration, queue/dependency admission and run ownership. Effects on a remote machine merely because an HTTP submission succeeded.
Agent runtime Model-decision progression, advertised tools, waits, observations and completion validation. External success based solely on model narration.
Execution engine and registered adapters Concrete argument preparation, schema checks, availability, permissions and operation dispatch. Permission from discovery or from text supplied by a model.
Gateway Target-local process/provider operations, jobs, cancellation and physical execution evidence. Which overall user goal the Agent should pursue next.
State and result owners Canonical task/run records, receipts, artifacts and recovery snapshots. Fresh external state from an old receipt or cached procedure.
Model routing and optional inference management Accepted model configuration and, in supported builds, managed endpoint processes. Authority to run a tool on a selected Gateway.

Application composition restores the Controller repository graph before constructing execution services, then starts reconciliation, checkpointing and background workers. RuntimeHost connects the model client, registry, execution engine and domain services. AgentLoop owns one run's progression lease and delegates decision acquisition, dispatch, recovery and publication to their existing owners. Concrete adapters call their service/provider boundaries.

From request to completion

  1. The request boundary validates submitted intent and resolves trusted context. Accepted work captures model routing, selected targets and applicable request settings; ordinary parameter references retain their accepted values. Queueing and dependency waits do not require a new model decision.
  2. Run initialization accepts or restores a checkpoint under a progression lease. The runtime builds model context and advertises tools within the permitted capability selection. Optional Task Contract Compilation prepares intent inside this same run owner; it is separate from the execution task board.
  3. The model proposes a response or tool call. The runtime validates the protocol, arguments, routing and current execution authority before dispatch. Exact bound parameters are materialized for the dispatch copy; the model journal retains their symbolic call. Controller-local operations stay local, while target work uses the selected Gateway.
  4. Actual results and receipts become the next observations. Jobs, dependencies, human replies, approvals and OAuth interactions can suspend progress at their existing boundaries. A machine wait does not spend inference calls merely to wait; an eligible continuation reacquires ownership before another decision.
  5. Completion checks evaluate the model's proposed outcome against required evidence and pending work. Publication derives the response, artifacts and UI state from accepted runtime facts. A failed or uncertain operation remains distinguishable from successful completion.

The evidence-based completion rule is REAL RESULT + RECEIPT: a proposed success is checked against actual results and the evidence required by its contract when the corresponding Agent Checks are enabled. Disabled verification is reported separately; model narration alone does not establish that an external effect occurred. The completion guide below distinguishes configurable checks from mandatory waits.

The request lifecycle follows individual transitions. Task admission owns queueing and held requests; scheduling distinguishes task, model, Activity and resource admission. Tool contracts and completion evidence describe invocation and terminal checks.

Policy, configuration and model boundaries

Capability discovery describes available tools; it does not grant permission to use them. ExecutionEngine prepares concrete inputs and rechecks live permission/resource authority at dispatch. Exact approvals, unsafe actions and accepted collaboration mode retain their own checks. Choosing Plan or Ask is distinct from changing a capability selection or Permission Policy; the UI tour explains those modes.

Model Configuration owns Main, Helper and optional Vision routes and generation settings. New tasks capture the applicable model configuration; accepted queued/resumed work retains its snapshot. Explicit product actions can use bounded drafting helpers, and configured monitors can judge observations. These helpers do not replace the Agent's ordinary decision loop.

The source registry in skills/catalog.py composes bundled skills explicitly. The generated Tool and Skill Reference is the current registration inventory; availability and selected capabilities can narrow what a particular run sees. Skill authoring describes how adapters fit these boundaries.

Inference management has a separate store and process supervisors. Build-owned feature identity enables it for supported Linux source runs and inference-enabled Server builds; configuration cannot activate it in an external-only package. Its Controller integration mounts the management surfaces and joins the existing application lifecycle. External model endpoints remain usable without Controller-owned inference management.

State, recovery and the UI

Core Controller repositories use the immutable RAM state hub. Runtime publication and a completed disk save are distinct boundaries: the checkpoint worker writes a complete recovery generation, and shutdown coordinates its final save. Retained standalone store implementations can use SQLite directly outside active hub ownership. The Gateway has its own execution and recovery authority. Read state and recovery and Server startup and shutdown before changing these owners.

A reconnecting browser projects server-owned work; closing a tab does not stop an accepted run. Pause, Stop, a human reply and service shutdown are different actions. Recovery reconciles persisted identities and physical evidence before further progress; transport uncertainty is not evidence that repeating an effect is safe. Artifacts and output projections retain their separate publication contracts.

Use the system flow map and sequence index to follow data across subsystem boundaries, the source map to locate a behavior and the repository package guide to navigate immediate files. Subsystem guides explain events and schedules, monitors, Workflows, parameter acceptance, attachments and Vision and command Working Context. Historical evidence remains in the manual's Historical group rather than serving as current setup instructions.
